name: Aurolab intraocular-lens production
description: Aurolab began producing intraocular lenses in India in 1992; reports place its early output at roughly 35,000 lenses.

impact.note: Cheap local manufacture of an existing lens widened cataract surgery for patients in poorer countries, with a few follow-on low-cost products.

date.label: Early production, 1992–1993
date.basis: WHO assigns nearly 35,000 to 1992; a separate case study places 35,000 in 1992–1993.

events.statement: Aurolab began producing intraocular lenses in India in 1992; reports place its early output at roughly 35,000 lenses.

evidence.locator: Jaipur Foot and intraocular lenses, pp. 54–56
evidence.supports: WHO dates Jaipur Foot development to 1968, reports free provision under BMVSS from 1975 and 59 limbs fitted in its first year. It reports Aurolab producing nearly 35,000 lenses in 1992 at roughly US$10 each. The counts are not patient counts and the cost is not necessarily a patient charge; a separate overview states US$5 on an unclear basis.
The case study reports 35,000 Aurolab lenses in 1992–1993; WHO reports nearly 35,000 in 1992.
Aravind authors report an initial US$10 per lens sale price, not an individual patient charge.

events.caveats: Reported production is not people treated. WHO reports approximately US$10 per lens in its detailed case study but US$5 in an overview without matching date or cost basis; neither is a documented patient charge. WHO assigns nearly 35,000 lenses to 1992; a separate case study reports 35,000 in 1992–1993, so the count cannot be assigned securely to the 1992 calendar year.
